# Introduction

We can use two sequences as querys to extract the genes from our
samples. The first is to download one COI and lsrDNA sequences 
from GenBank. The second is to use the extracted genes from the 
draft genome we assembled.

Additionally, we construct two phylogenetic trees to see the
relationships between the samples.

## Getting the sequences from GenBank
I'm going to test several COI markers obtained from GenBank and Isabel. We don't know if 
there are more than one species in our samples, so I'm going to test the COI from C. farionis and 
C. pseudofarionis. Since the same gene can not be mapped at the same time, I need to create a specific 
folder for each marker. At the end, I'm gonna leave the code in README, but without executation, only 
keeping the chosen marker.

```{bash, collapse=TRUE}
# From NCBI:
if [ ! -d markers ]; then mkdir markers; fi
for ACCESSION in MW729433 OL763881 MT080780 MW368672 OP580487 MT080786 MT080758 MT080768; do
  BROWSER="https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=nuccore&id="
  TYPE="&rettype=fasta&retmode=text"
  if [ ! -e markers/$ACCESSION.fa ]; then
    curl -s $BROWSER$ACCESSION$TYPE -o markers/${ACCESSION}.fa
  fi
done
```


## Abreviations for the sequences 
 
```{bash}
cd markers
#Cox1
if [ ! -e COI_MW_Cfar.fa ]; then mv MW729433.fa COI_MW_Cfar.fa && sed -i '1s/.*/>COI_MW_Cfar/' COI_MW_Cfar.fa; fi #far Vainutis
if [ ! -e COI_OL_Cfar.fa ]; then mv OL763881.fa COI_OL_Cfar.fa && sed -i '1s/.*/>COI_OL_Cfar/' COI_OL_Cfar.fa; fi #far Atopkin

#28S
if [ ! -e lsrDNA_MT_Cfar.fa ]; then mv MT080780.fa lsrDNA_MT_Cfar.fa && sed -i '1s/.*/>lsrDNA_MT_Cfar/' lsrDNA_MT_Cfar.fa; fi #far Faltynkova
if [ ! -e lsrDNA_MW_Cfar.fa ]; then mv MW368672.fa lsrDNA_MW_Cfar.fa && sed -i '1s/.*/>lsrDNA_MW_Cfar/' lsrDNA_MW_Cfar.fa; fi #far Vainutis

if [ ! -e lsrDNA_OP_Cpse.fa ]; then mv OP580487.fa lsrDNA_OP_Cpse.fa && sed -i '1s/.*/>lsrDNA_OP_Cpse/' lsrDNA_OP_Cpse.fa; fi #far Rochart
if [ ! -e lsrDNA_MT_Cpse.fa ]; then mv MT080786.fa lsrDNA_MT_Cpse.fa && sed -i '1s/.*/>lsrDNA_MT_Cpse/' lsrDNA_MT_Cpse.fa; fi #pse Faltynkova

#ITS2
if [ ! -e ITS2_MT_Cfar.fa ]; then mv MT080758.fa ITS2_MT_Cfar.fa && sed -i '1s/.*/>ITS2_MT_Cfar/' ITS2_MT_Cfar.fa; fi #far Faltynkova
if [ ! -e ITS2_MT_Cpse.fa ]; then mv MT080768.fa ITS2_MT_Cpse.fa && sed -i '1s/.*/>ITS2_MT_Cpse/' ITS2_MT_Cpse.fa; fi #far Faltynkova

cd ..
```

# Mapping of ddRAD-seq reads to *cox1* and *lsrDNA* genes

```{bash}

PATHFQ=/nata/joiglu/crepidostomum2/results/2023-05-17/crepi_edits

for REF in COI_MW_Cfar COI_OL_Cfar COI_Cfar COI_Cpse lsrDNA_MT_Cfar lsrDNA_MW_Cfar lsrDNA_OP_Cpse lsrDNA_MT_Cpse ITS2_MT_Cfar ITS2_MT_Cpse; do
  if [ ! -d BAM_$REF ]; then mkdir BAM_$REF; fi
  if [ ! -e markers/$REF.0123 ]; then
     bwa-mem2 index markers/${REF}.fa
  fi

  #bwa-mem2 index $COX
  for i in $(ls $PATHFQ/*.trimmed_R1_.fastq.gz); do
     SAMPLE=$(basename $i .trimmed_R1_.fastq.gz)
     if [ ! -e BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.bam ]; then
        if [ ! -e BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.sam ]; then
           # I skip "pairing" (-P) and avoid "mate rescue" (-S), to map forward
           # and reverse reads independently.
           bwa-mem2 mem -t 24 -P -S markers/${REF}.fa ${PATHFQ}/${SAMPLE}.trimmed_R1_.fastq.gz \
                                   ${PATHFQ}/${SAMPLE}.trimmed_R2_.fastq.gz \
                        -R "@RG\tID:${SAMPLE}\tSM:${SAMPLE}" > BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.sam &
        fi
        wait
        # We expect very few reads to map on cox1 or lsrDNA, and don't need to
        # save the rest in the bam. Thus, I filter the umapped reads.
        samtools view -q 20 -F 4 -u BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.sam | \
        samtools sort > BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.bam
        samtools index BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.bam
        rm BAM_$REF/${SAMPLE}.sam
     fi
  done
done
```

## Extract a consensus sequences for each BAM file 
First of all, I remove those samples that not interest us, the bad samples with many
Ns and low data, and all of them belongs to the Alpine region.

The samples are: T165Cxa, N048Cma, N048Cmb, N048Cmc, N044Cx2

```{bash}
for sample in N048Cmc N048Cma N048Cmb N044Cx2 T165Cxa; do
  find ./ -name "${sample}.bam.bai" | xargs rm
  find ./ -name "${sample}.bam" | xargs rm
done 
```

```{bash}
if [ ! -d GB ]; then mkdir GB; fi
for REF in COI_MW_Cfar COI_OL_Cfar COI_Cfar COI_Cpse lsrDNA_MT_Cfar lsrDNA_MW_Cfar lsrDNA_OP_Cpse lsrDNA_MT_Cpse ITS2_MT_Cfar ITS2_MT_Cpse; do
  if [ ! -e GB/${REF}_align.fa ]; then
    for bam in $(ls -1 BAM_$REF/*.bam); do
      SAMPLE=$(basename -s .bam $bam)
      samtools consensus -r $REF $bam -A --P-het 0 \
                         -l 2000 -a --show-del yes --show-ins no | \
      sed "s/>${REF}/>${SAMPLE}/" | \
      sed "s/*/-/g" >> GB/${REF}_align.fa
    done
  fi
done

```


## Phylogenetic reconstruction

Filter and trim the alignments with Gblocks 
```{bash}
for COI in COI_MW_Cfar_align.fa COI_OL_Cfar_align.fa COI_Cfar_align.fa COI_Cpse_align.fa; do 
  #if [ ! -e GB/$COI-gb1 ]; then
     Gblocks GB/$COI -t=d -b1=46 -b2=60 -b4=10 -e=-gb1 -d=y -v=1000 -b3=10 -b5=h
  #fi
done

for lsrDNA in lsrDNA_MT_Cfar_align.fa lsrDNA_MW_Cfar_align.fa lsrDNA_OP_Cpse_align.fa lsrDNA_MT_Cpse_align.fa; do 
  #if [ ! -e GB/$lsrDNA-gb1 ]; then
     Gblocks GB/$lsrDNA -t=d -b1=65 -b2=91 -b4=10 -e=-gb1 -d=y -v=1500 -b3=50 -b5=h
  #fi
done

for ITS in ITS2_MT_Cfar_align.fa ITS2_MT_Cpse_align.fa; do 
  #if [ ! -e GB/$ITS-gb1 ]; then
     Gblocks GB/$ITS -t=d -b1=59 -b2=80 -b4=10 -e=-gb1 -d=y -v=1000 -b3=10 -b5=h
  #fi
done
```

# Conclusions
Since all the markers of COI maps aprox. the same name of sequences, 
that are very low in all cases, we choose the marker from GenBank, 
COI_MW_Cfar - MW729433 from Russia. 
For lsrDNA, the sequences aligned with the markers are so much more long, 
and the mapping is again very similar across the markers tested, so we 
choose the marker form GenBank lsrDNA_MT_Cpse - MT080786 from Iceland, the
one with the longest fragments extracted. 

For ITS2, the sequences aligned with the markers are so empty, and the 
number of base pairs once aligned, was very low. Still, we choose he 
marker from GenBank ITS2_MT_Cpse - MT080768 from Iceland
